items.mechanised: yes — #295: `cancel-in-progress: false` on `.github/workflows/pr-hygiene.yml` and `.github/workflows/browser-qa.yml`. A run cancelled while still *pending* creates no job and no check run (runs 35613803628 and 35613803591: `completed/cancelled`, `jobs: 0`, absent from the commit's check-runs), so GitHub still collapses the queue to one pending run per group and the failure mode is gone rather than rarer — at the cost of one extra run per PR and no cancellation of a superseded push. Narrowing `types:` was rejected: both checks genuinely depend on labels. Guarded by `scripts/required-checks.logic.mjs`; recovery for PRs opened before it landed is in `docs/harness/README.md` § When a required check is stuck

items.whatWentWrong: The layer ratchet — the foundation plan's one tracked metric and the guard the whole refactor leans on — could be reset by a documented command with nothing watching. Measured today on `main`: one new `src/core` → `src/store` import fails `pnpm run lint:layers`; `pnpm exec depcruise src --config .dependency-cruiser.cjs --baseline` then exits 0, the baseline goes 72 rows → 73, the edge is absorbed and `lint` is green again. `shrink-only` refuses the same edge (stays 72), but nothing exposed or blocked the full write, no CI job ran it, the file has no CODEOWNERS, and `.gitattributes` marks it `linguist-generated` so no one line-reviews its rows in a PR. The only fence was a prose paragraph in the config, and the command it warns about is the same one a legitimate rule-arming needs (#404 took the baseline 34 → 77 arming `core-through-index`)
items.shouldHaveBeenCaughtBy: nothing could: `lint` runs on the PR head and sees one baseline, so it cannot tell growth from a rewrite; the size budget deliberately excludes the file; and review cannot read a 737-line machine-written diff. The check had to be **base-aware**, which only the `pull_request_target` surface is
items.mechanised: yes — #406: the `ratchet` rule in `scripts/pr-hygiene.logic.mjs` reads the baseline at the PR's merge base and at the head and fails any row added under a rule name that already existed, naming the rows. Growth under a new rule name with nothing removed passes (#404's real 34 → 77 is a test); the count gates nothing, so fixing one violation while absorbing another fails too (#432's verification — it warned at first, and that is the ordinary shape of a refactor that moves files between layers); rows leaving *and* arriving under a new rule name warns, since a rule renamed in the config is the same shape as an arming in the baseline and only the config line fences it; and a `Baseline-growth:` declaration that **names every row it excuses** turns a fail into a warn on the record. `linguist-generated` stays — the file is rewritten whole, so a line review sees churn — and `.gitattributes` and the config header now say that this rule is what pays for the lost review. `eslint-suppressions.json` has the same hole (#360's verifier) and is #429

items.whatWentWrong: The guard written for the row above passed its own attack. `#406`'s criterion was "a row may only appear under a rule name **new in this PR**"; the code derived "new" from the base *baseline rows*, and `engine-no-ui-packages` is armed in `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` with 0 of the 72 rows. So a real `zustand` import under `src/core/` plus the documented `depcruise … --baseline` write (72 → 73) read `PASS ratchet=armed`, "arming `engine-no-ui-packages` (1 row)", exit 0 — with **no config edit**, no declaration and nothing reviewable; an invented rule name passed the same way, and the same case plus one repaired violation read `WARN ratchet=swapped`, sending the reader to a config diff that did not exist. The channel widened as the ratchet succeeded: `engine-no-ui` is down to one row, `state-no-3d` and `src-no-e2e` to two
items.shouldHaveBeenCaughtBy: the test that claimed to cover it — `pr-hygiene.logic.test.mjs`'s "growth under a rule name new in this PR" — supplied no config at all, so it encoded the same conflation as the code and could never have failed on it. A criterion and its implementation used two different definitions of one term, and the only thing that could have caught the gap was a case where they disagree: a rule present in the config and absent from the baseline
items.mechanised: yes — #432 round 3: `armed` and `swapped` now require the rule name to be declared in the head `.dependency-cruiser.cjs`, absent from the base copy, and that file to be among the PR's own changed files, so a claim of arming always costs a reviewable line. The `main-rules` ruleset could only be merged through by admin bypass (1 approval a solo owner cannot give; `required_deployments` and `code_scanning` rules no PR could satisfy); AGENTS.md claimed CI was required — it was not
First research draft kept the owner as the merge bottleneck and proposed label gates the owner's own identity defeats

Tracer PR #238: the pre-commit `tsc -b` makes a compile-broken "red" commit impossible; the builder committed the test file from a green tree instead
`pnpm install` in every worktree prints `husky: command not found` (husky is not a devDependency; hooks still run via `core.hooksPath`)

Issue #149's verification command named an exact new test file (`scripts/backlog.test.mjs`); the builder followed the repo's `x.logic.test.mjs` convention, so the command as written exited 1

`strict` up-to-date policy: every PR needs a rebase + fresh CI (~2 min) once `main` moves; with three PRs landing in an hour that was three extra CI runs
`pr-hygiene` was made a required check after being tried only on human PRs; every dependabot PR then failed its linked-issue rule
Removing the admin bypass broke every release: `@semantic-release/git` pushes a commit to `main`, now rejected (`GH013`); five release runs failed before anyone looked
The agents' `gh` token lacked the `workflow` scope, so they could not update or auto-merge any PR touching `.github/workflows/**` (dependabot #118/#131, and a cosmetic `ci.yml` hunk in #245)
`strict` required-status-checks made every merge put every other green PR `BEHIND`; ten PRs in two hours meant a rebase + CI cycle each, and dependabot PRs re-triggered each other
PR #244 added an AGENTS.md line citing `pr-hygiene.logic.mjs` without its `scripts/` prefix; the path-exists check (#245) caught it as soon as its branch was rebased onto that `main`
The eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 bump (dependabot #114) failed lint with four real "Cannot access refs during render" findings
The browser-qa builder kept polling its own CI after its PR merged (~300k tokens)
A builder's `git fetch` hung (a ref-lock race with another worktree fetching at the same moment); the agent sat idle until it was stopped and resumed
The default subagent model was switched to Sonnet to cut cost without asking; the owner corrected it (Opus for significant work, Sonnet only for routine work)

The first cloud-spike routine did all its work, then could not push (403: the Claude GitHub App had no write access), so its commit died with the container
Connecting Cursor to GitHub switched on Bugbot (billed per use) for every PR without the owner finding the setting; it reviewed #294

The definition of done had drifted past the three versions on record: a grep found ten live restatements (`CLAUDE.md` ×2, `AGENTS.md` ×2, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `REPO_MAP.md`, `docs/llm-docs-sync.md`, `docs/roadmap/README.md`, `verifier-brief.md`), one down to two commands with `build` missing entirely

The mechanism, read off the API rather than guessed: GitHub sends one webhook action **per label**, so `gh pr edit --add-label a,b` right after `gh pr create` delivers `opened`, `labeled`, `labeled` in the same second or two and starts three `pr-hygiene` and three `browser-qa` runs; `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels one mid-run, a run cancelled *in progress* posts a `cancelled` check run under the required context name, and GitHub judges a required context by the **newest** check run with that name — so `gh pr checks` reads all green while `mergeStateStatus` stays `BLOCKED`

#326's deletion-only exemption met its first real deletion (#321 + #332) and did not apply: the same issue that asks for ~1,050 deleted lines also asks for the guard that keeps them deleted, and that guard is 194 lines across two files — past the ≤ 5-lines-per-file fix-up proxy — so `pr-hygiene` read FAIL at 523 reviewable lines, 517 of them deletions

Recovering #295's stuck required checks by rerunning every cancelled run at once **made it worse** — each rerun contends with its sibling under the same `concurrency` group, and on #362 one cancellation became three. The coordinator's own written recovery advice was the cause, and it had never been tried under contention before being written down
